svg.title: The log is flushed first. That is why "none" survives a power cut.
svg.desc: A transaction box with BEGIN at the top and COMMIT at the bottom containing a debit of 50 000 and a matching credit, struck by a red lightning bolt labelled kill -9. The balances before and after the crash are identical at 100 000 each. Below, a numbered pair of steps shows the write-ahead log record being fsynced first and the data pages written later, with the reversed order crossed out in red.
svg.text: The log is flushed first. That is why "none" survives a power cut.
the money came back. Nothing was
write the intent to the LOG, and fsync it
write the data PAGES later, lazily
BEGIN ... call the payment API ... COMMIT
you now hold locks for someone else's outage
3 000 inserts as 3 000 commits: 2 571 ms vs one transaction: 886 ms (2.9x)
...and if the two writes are in two different databases?
